extraction.name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) dataset
extraction.description: A large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research, derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox, consisting of 8 languages with about 44.5K hours of English and about 6K hours for other languages.
extraction.creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert
extraction.citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411v2, 2020.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox, which are based on Project Gutenberg text data. Audio files are downloaded and segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models. Pseudo labels are generated via beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model. Text sources are downloaded from various domains (e.g., gutenberg.org, archive.org) and manually searched for invalid links. Text normalization is performed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For audiobooks with invalid links for text sources, manual online search was conducted to find alternate sources. Some audiobooks were excluded if text sources could not be obtained.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LibriVox audiobooks and Project Gutenberg text data.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Numbers in text are replaced with aligned words from pseudo labels. Hyphens and apostrophes are handled using heuristics based on word rarity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Audio segmented into 10-20 second segments. Text normalization: NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters, removal of end-of-line hyphens, filtering characters based on language orthography. Candidate transcripts filtered if WER > 40%.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Transcripts are generated automatically via alignment of pseudo labels with source text using TF-IDF and Smith-Waterman alignment. For development and test sets, human transcribers listen to audio and correct 'clear and obvious' errors in transcripts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human transcribers were asked to only correct 'clear and obvious' errors to avoid adding potential bias. WER between generated transcript and human rated transcript is reported (e.g., English dev 4.55%, test 4.54%).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Acoustic models (TDS convolutions with ASG loss), beam-search decoder with 4-gram LM, TF-IDF, Smith-Waterman alignment, KenLM toolkit for language models.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be made freely available at http://www.openslr.org. Language models and baseline ASR models are also released.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender labels for speakers are inferred using a classifier trained on LibriSpeech data. No explicit personal sensitive information is collected.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential biases: gender classifier accuracy varies by language (e.g., 96% on Dutch, 94% on Polish). The dataset is derived from audiobooks, which may reflect certain demographics and reading styles.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is read speech, not conversational. Some languages have limited hours (e.g., Polish 103.65 hours). High OOV rate for Polish (13.39%) negatively impacts LM decoding. Development and test sets are chosen to be harder than LibriSpeech dev/test-other.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and test sets for ASR and TTS research. Limited supervision subsets (10h, 1h, 10-minute sets) for low-resource benchmarks.
